summary: A dense, puzzly worker-placement-adjacent game where the six actions on the shifting 'crane' constantly change in cost and reward, so most of the game is spent reading the current board state and chaining a few efficient moves before the setup shifts again. It rewards engine-building and tight optimization over direct interaction, with construction of the bridge, city walls, and cathedral providing the scoring backbone.
praised: Clever, tightly-interlocking action system where the crane's shifting costs/rewards create constant fresh puzzles
High replayability due to variable setup and multiple viable strategies
Strong sense of progression and engine-building satisfaction
Elegant hexagonal tile-laying for New Prague City
Manages its complexity without feeling bloated once learned
criticised: Steep learning curve and a lot of upfront rules/iconography to absorb
Can feel more solitaire/multiplayer-solitaire than interactive
Analysis paralysis potential given the many interlocking sub-systems
Some find the theme pasted-on to what is fundamentally an abstract optimization puzzle

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light area-majority competition for building spots

scoring.why: Points accumulate from multiple construction projects (city tiles, bridge, walls, cathedral), resource/action-strength efficiency, and end-game bonuses, so the winner is decided by whoever builds the most efficient overall engine rather than one dominant source
